You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC observations

## Task 493a67b3 — fill enclosed cavities in outlined color-6 shapes
- Background is 9; outlines/objects are color 6. Recolor enclosed interior cells to 4, preserving every outline and all other background.
- Demo 1 used color 1 outlines on background 0. A roughly rectangular outlined loop at rows 14–20, cols 16–18 enclosed a one-cell-wide cavity at column 17, rows 15–19; output changed those cavity cells to 4. The loop had an attached horizontal extension, which did not alter the fill.
- Test had three cavities: shape at rows 9–12, cols 0–4 -> fill rows 10–11, cols 1–3; vertical outlined shape at rows 8–13, cols 6–8 -> fill rows 9–12, col 7; both filled with 4. Accepted after an initial wrong output that forgot the bottom cavity cell (r12,c7).
- General rule: find hollow/closed outline regions and fill only the enclosed background-color cells with 4; don't fill exterior/background or replace borders. Attached extensions can be present.

## Task a130a2b4
Solved the test after one demo. The grid contains several large monochrome rectangular/irregular regions amid background color 7. Isolated foreign-color pixels are distractor/noise: erase them to the local region's color when inside a region, and to background 7 when outside. Preserve the base shapes and background patches. Demo confirmed this: within the large color-3 and color-0 fields, isolated 9/2/6 markers were changed to the surrounding fill; an isolated 9 in the top-left 3-field was likewise removed. In test, preserve 5 and 9 regions, clean stray marker values (2/4/8/0/3) according to the region/background beneath them, and keep unrelated colored rectangular patches that form coherent regions (e.g. the 9 blocks at lower left and far right).

# Continual-ARC observed rule

For grids partitioned by full-width horizontal lines and full-height vertical lines of a separator color, process each resulting rectangular region independently. Ignore separator lines. The output is a smaller grid with one cell per region, in the same layout/order. Set that cell to `1` iff the region contains exactly two cells of the sparse marker color; otherwise set it to the region's background color.

Evidence: task-b5438fdd demos used marker colors 4 and 5, separator colors 6 and 3, and backgrounds 7 and 0. In both, regions with exactly two marker cells mapped to 1; regions with a different count mapped to the background. On the solved test, separator=5, background=4, marker=7; each 4x3 region maps according to the same rule, yielding `[[4,1],[4,1],[4,4]]`.
